extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, BBC executives, broadcast editors, journalists, and senior civil servants
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and normative guidance for broadcast/investigative journalism, BBC governance, and civil-servant/media interactions in high‑stakes public-interest reporting (as discussed in the Hutton report debate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous source verification and scepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced journalists test their sources rigorously. They proceed with watchful scepticism, scrutinising the emerging information from every angle, build up knowledge through further inquiry, put the allegations to those involved and painstakingly build up the fullest possible picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always verify claims via multiple avenues, challenge and cross-check sources, give subjects an opportunity to respond, and avoid relying on a single tip or uncorroborated assertion. Anti-pattern: broadcasting unverified allegations based on a single, unchecked source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and legal scrutiny for grave allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: When grave allegations are to be made—and especially when there is a risk of libel—the programme's senior editorial staff need to bring into play the organisation's best editorial and legal minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalate potential libel/serious public- interest stories to senior editors and legal counsel before broadcast/publication. Document legal sign‑offs and advice. Anti-pattern: allowing a reporter to publish serious charges without senior editorial/legal involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due editorial oversight of reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme failed to exercise due editorial scrutiny over its reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial teams must supervise reporters' investigations, verify their work, and intervene when reporting standards lapse. Ensure mechanisms for supervision, mentoring and checks on junior or trusted reporters alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and rigorous internal investigation when coverage is challenged
rubrics_metrics.description: When the coverage was challenged, it should have been rigorously investigated by BBC executives. Instead there was blind defence and sophistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On credible challenge, conduct swift, transparent internal reviews rather than reflexive defence. Establish clear procedures and timelines for investigating complaints or challenges to reporting. Anti-pattern: delay or defensive posture that deepens institutional damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit of truth and journalistic integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism that is honestly engaged in the pursuit of truth—journalism that is rigorous, fair-minded and questioning; journalism that is committed to getting it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that absolute truth may be unattainable, but prioritise honest, fair, and thorough reporting. Value context and balance; correct errors promptly. Scoring note: integrity includes both process (rigour) and outcome (accuracy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance independence with safeguarding integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The independence of the BBC … is sacred. Of course the BBC must be willing to stand up to the powerful. Of course it must investigate and reveal. But the governors' failure—under fire—was not to focus at the same time on another, equally vital, principle: the need to safeguard the integrity of the BBC's journalism, to try to discover whether the story complained of was actually true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect editorial independence while ensuring editorial processes actually sustain truthful, verifiable journalism. Governance should defend independence but also demand standards and truth-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely governance and regulatory action
rubrics_metrics.description: They took far too long to exert a grip as the crisis rumbled on. They failed for too long to act as the BBC's regulators—and, in the process, they have brought into question the institution's 1920s system of governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governors/regulators must act promptly to investigate and resolve crises, and governance structures should be modernised to provide effective oversight. Delayed responses exacerbate reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not stretch or massage uncertain evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: It had to make uncertain evidence carry more weight than it was capable of bearing. The charge is that the Government stretched the evidence, that it massaged the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present uncertainty transparently; avoid turning tenuous or speculative findings into definitive claims. Explicitly label best-case/worst-case scenarios and the limits of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear guidelines on civil servants' media access (no grey areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an urgent need for very clear guidelines to be set out on where civil servants have access to the media. There is no room for any grey areas. ... the code of conduct for civil servants envisaged under Clause 13 of the Bill places the situation beyond all reasonable doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish unambiguous rules for when and how civil servants may speak to media, and the procedures for authorisation and record-keeping. Ensure training and internal communications clarify these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of care and protection of civil servants
rubrics_metrics.description: To have exposed Dr David Kelly to intense media interest is greatly to be regretted and must never be allowed to happen to a civil servant again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with named/unnamed civil servants connected to sensitive reporting, actively consider anonymity, welfare and duty-of-care obligations. Anti-pattern: public statements that foreseeably lead to identification and exposure of vulnerable officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use leak and internal inquiries properly; avoid bypassing channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The information that Dr Kelly had volunteered should, as Dr Wells pointed out, have been made available to the leak inquiry, but it bypassed it and we still do not really know why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route allegations through established leak/investigation channels so that internal processes can assess and act appropriately before public escalation. Document rationale if bypassing established routes is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of the media balanced with protection from false accusations (responsible journalism/Reynolds principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication by the media of information (including information obtained by investigative reporters) on matters of public interest and importance is a vital part of life in a democratic society. However the right to communicate such information is subject to the qualification … that false accusations of fact impugning the integrity of others, including politicians, should not be made by the media. … The common law does not seek to set a higher standard than that of responsible journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect investigative reporting on matters of public interest, but ensure responsible practices (verification, fairness, right of reply) to benefit from qualified legal defences (e.g., Reynolds-style responsible journalism). Anti-pattern: reckless allegations without attempting to verify or offer respondents a chance to answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vet and trust reporters before granting broad freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC must be able to trust its reporters before it can give them that freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reporters' track records and provide oversight correspondingly; freedom to report should be matched by demonstrated reliability. If indicators of unreliability exist, increase editorial checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply equivalent standards to government communications and the media
rubrics_metrics.description: It cannot be right to apply a lower standard to the Government than we apply to the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold government public communications (e.g., dossiers) to the same standards of accuracy, transparency and accountability as the media. Scrutinise official claims and require clarity on evidence and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: release inquiry materials where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: I am glad that they have been released as it has been an exercise in open government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible and consistent with privacy/security, publish inquiry documents and evidence to enable public scrutiny and accountability. Use appropriate redaction when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding model should preserve public-service journalism and arts, not subsidies for entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: I would like someone to find a way of financing the BBC by a progressive tax, not a regressive tax. I would like to see the BBC protected for its journalism and its arts, but not for its entertainment. I do not see why I have to pay for BBC entertainment at all. It can go out and compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design funding mechanisms that prioritise public-service journalism and cultural content, consider fairness of funding burden, and allow entertainment to operate in competitive marketplaces.
